# FDG9076

> DO NOT let exceptions escape from the finalizer logic, except for system-critical failures.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.4.2 Finalizable Types.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1065
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1065 reports an exception created directly in a finalizer, in a type of any accessibility (probe with SDK 10.0.402). Exceptions from methods that the finalizer calls, such as Dispose(false), are not seen, and neither is the finalizer code path inside Dispose(bool), so coverage is partial; the system-critical failures the text excepts cannot be told apart. CA1821 reports a finalizer whose only statement is a throw as empty (probe); it is not mapped. CA1065 is shared with FDG9069 and the chapter 5 and 8 rules listed there. Not throwing changes no signature; CA1065 has no code fix.

## From the book

If an exception is thrown from a finalizer, the CLR will shut down the entire process, preventing other finalizers from executing and resources from being released in a controlled manner.
